speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your dizziness, can you describe whether the sensation is that the room is spinning around you or if it feels like you might faint? Also, does this sensation get worse when you change your head position, such as rolling over in bed?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any ringing in your ears or a feeling of fullness in one ear during these dizzy spells? Also, have you noticed any weakness or numbness on one side of your body, or any difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you do not have ear symptoms like ringing or hearing loss changes, this points away from Meniere's disease. I will now examine your eye movements to check for nystagmus. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver confirms a diagnosis of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). I will now perform the Epley maneuver to reposition the displaced otoliths in your right ear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
